newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya Finance Bank to be liquidated.
newsitem.headline: Kenya Finance Bank to be liquidated.

text.p: Kenya Finance Bank, placed under Central Bank of Kenya statutory management in July, has been shut down, liquidators said on Wednesday.

Michael Cherwon, director of the Deposit Protection Fund Board, said the central bank had appointed his board official liquidator of the collapsed bank and payments to 29,222 protected small depositors would begin on January 6, 1997.
The bank had a total of 31,195 depositors. Under Kenyan law, deposits of up to 100,000 shillings ($1,790) are protected.
Kenya Finance Bank was put under statutory management after its prolonged failure to meet liquidity and cash ratio rules.
Cash ratio, at 18 percent, is the total cash a commercial bank must deposit with the central bank at no interest.

"A statutory manager was appointed and after examining its books found that the institution was basically insolvent and in the situation, the obvious option was to liquidate," Central Bank of Kenya Governor Micah Cheserem said in a statement.

Cheserem said the option of reopening the bank failed because the manager he appointed was not able to sell its assets to raise 400 million shillings ($7.14 million) required to pay small depositors. He added that the loan portfolio was non-performing due to poor lending policies of the bank's previous management.
Cheserem has previously said that the collapse of a poorly run institution such as the Kenya Finance Bank did not in any way lower investor confidence in the financial bodies in Kenya.

Cheserem, 47 and deeply reform-minded, has tried to instil greater financial discipline and has instituted better monitoring of the operations and management of commercial banks since he was appointed to head the central bank in 1993.

At least five directors of the Kenya Finance Bank have been charged in court with fraud-related crimes. The prosecution says the directors consented to or published annual reports showing the bank to be performing well when in fact it was nearing collapse.
